output.answer: Walmart runs one of the largest private retail supply chains in the world: per its fiscal 2026 10-K (year ended Jan 31, 2026) it sources from a global base of U.S. and international suppliers and moves merchandise through 192 U.S. distribution facilities and 179 facilities abroad (Africa, Canada, Central America, Chile, China, India, Mexico), using its own private truck fleet plus common carriers, with most merchandise shipped through those facilities and the rest shipped directly from suppliers to its more than 10,900 stores and clubs. In 2026 it pushed three big changes: a "Prepaid Consolidation" first-mile program (announced May 26, 2026) that funnels supplier shipments into automated consolidation centers before redistributing across its 42 U.S. regional distribution centers; an expanded commercial agreement with Symbotic (Oct 29, 2026) to deploy AI-powered warehouse automation across 25 U.S. regional distribution centers backed by an initial $6 billion commitment plus $125 million of R&D; and continued last-mile expansion — including its fifth next-generation fulfillment center (900,000+ sq ft, Stockton, CA, Oct 8, 2026) and a multi-year Zipline deal (Nov 5, 2026) adding 300 drone delivery sites on top of more than 2 million drone deliveries completed. During fiscal 2026 Walmart also merged the Sam's Club U.S. supply chain function into Walmart U.S. to streamline operations, and it fulfills e-commerce orders from stores, clubs, eCommerce fulfillment centers and other distribution facilities, offering same-day pickup and delivery at substantially all U.S. stores.
caveats: The 192 U.S. and 179 international distribution-facility counts are as of the fiscal 2026 10-K (year ended Jan 31, 2026); Walmart opens and converts facilities frequently (e.g. the Stockton fulfillment center opened Oct 2026), so exact counts change.

The Symbotic $6 billion figure is an initial multi-year commitment described in Symbotic's announcement and a securities filing as reported by Supply Chain Dive; deployment pace and scope across the 25 regional distribution centers could change.
The Zipline drone expansion is a multi-year rollout 'with potential to expand'; site availability and delivery speed ('as fast as 30 minutes') apply only where the service operates.
The Prepaid Consolidation program 'will scale in phases' with participation prioritized by volume alignment and capacity, so not all suppliers are covered yet.

passages.quote: We continue to invest in supply chain automation and our fulfillment and delivery capabilities to better serve our customers. In the U.S., we utilize a network of 192 distribution facilities located strategically throughout the country using a combination of our private truck fleet as well as contracting with common carriers. During fiscal 2026, we began combining the Sam's Club U.S. supply chain function with Walmart U.S. to streamline operations and leverage our enterprise systems and infrastructure over time. Outside the U.S., we utilize a total of 179 distribution facilities strategically located in Africa, Canada, Central America, Chile, China, India and Mexico, which process and distribute both imported and domestic products to where our customers live. For fiscal 2026, the majority of our purchases of store and club merchandise were shipped through these facilities, while most of the remaining merchandise we purchased was shipped directly from suppliers to our stores and clubs. As an omnichannel retailer, we ship merchandise purchased by customers on our eCommerce platforms by a number of methods from multiple locations, including leveraging our network of stores and clubs to fulfill and deliver customer orders, as well as shipping directly from eCommerce fulfillment centers and other distribution facilities.

Suppliers, Supply Chain and Distribution. As a retailer and warehouse club operator, we utilize a global supply chain that includes both U.S. and international suppliers from whom we purchase the merchandise that we sell in our stores, clubs and online. In many instances, we purchase merchandise from producers located near the stores and clubs in which such merchandise will be sold, particularly perishable items. Consistent with applicable laws, we offer our suppliers the opportunity to efficiently sell significant quantities of their products to us. These relationships enable us to obtain pricing that reflects the volume, certainty and cost-effectiveness these arrangements provide to such suppliers, which in turn enables us to provide low prices to our customers. Our suppliers are subject to standards of conduct, including requirements that they comply with local labor laws, local worker safety laws and other applicable laws. Our ability to acquire from our suppliers the assortment and volume of products we wish to offer to our customers, to receive those products within the required time through our supply chain and to distribute those products to our stores and clubs, determines, along with other supply chain logistics matters (such as containers or port access for example), in part, our in-stock levels in our stores and clubs and the attractiveness of our merchandise assortment we offer to our customers and members.

**BENTONVILLE, Ark., May 26, 2026** — Continuing its commitment of Everyday Low Prices (EDLP) for customers, Walmart today announced a new supply chain strategy, Prepaid Consolidation. This program helps get products to shelves and customers faster by simplifying inbound supplier logistics and building a more connected, scalable, tech-enabled supply chain that improves service and lowers costs.

The program expands Walmart’s first mile capabilities for prepaid suppliers by using its national supply chain network to create a scalable way to merge shipments, creating greater transportation efficiency. Suppliers send products under a single national purchase order to one location, and from there Walmart combines the inventory and distributes it across its 42 regional distribution centers (RDCs).

**WILMINGTON, Mass. (October 29, 2026) –** [Symbotic Inc.](https://www.symbotic.com/) (Nasdaq: [SYM](https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/stocks/sym)), a leader in A.I.-enabled robotics technology for the supply chain, and [Walmart Inc.](https://corporate.walmart.com/) (Nasdaq: [WMT](https://www.nyse.com/quote/XNGS:WMT)) today announced an expanded commercial agreement to bring further automation capabilities to 25 U.S. regional distribution centers, while supporting additional opportunities across Walmart’s global supply chain network.

**STOCKTON, Calif., Oct. 8, 2026** — Walmart today opened its fifth next-generation fulfillment center, a more than 900,000-square-foot facility in Stockton that will create more than 1,000 jobs and expand the retailer’s ability to provide faster shipping and delivery to customers across California and the West Coast.

The new facility represents the latest step in Walmart’s transformation of its supply chain, bringing associates together with advanced automation, technology and machine learning to move products faster and more efficiently. The technology enables Walmart to materially improve storage capacity and increase the number of customer orders the facility can fulfill each day compared with a traditional fulfillment center.

*   Expanding Nationwide: Walmart is adding 300 new Zipline drone delivery sites through a multi-year agreement, bringing faster delivery to more communities across the country.
*   Building on Momentum: With more than 2 million drone deliveries completed, Walmart is expanding a service designed to deliver everyday essentials in as fast as 30 minutes.
*   Convenience at Customers’ Fingertips: Eligible customers can shop tens of thousands of items through the Walmart app or Walmart.com and have orders delivered directly to their homes.

**BENTONVILLE, Ark., Nov. 5, 2026** — Walmart, which operates the nation’s largest retail drone delivery program, is bringing the delivery option to even more doorsteps. Today, the retailer announced a new multi-year agreement with Zipline to add 300 drone delivery sites nationwide, with the potential to expand. The rollout builds on Walmart’s drone delivery program, which has completed more than 2 million deliveries to date. Walmart has worked with Zipline to make drone deliveries since 2021.

key_facts.fact: In the U.S., Walmart uses a network of 192 distribution facilities served by its private truck fleet and common carriers; outside the U.S. it uses 179 distribution facilities in Africa, Canada, Central America, Chile, China, India and Mexico.

Walmart purchases merchandise from both U.S. and international suppliers; most store/club merchandise was shipped through its distribution facilities, while most of the remaining merchandise was shipped directly from suppliers to stores and clubs.
During fiscal 2026 Walmart began combining the Sam's Club U.S. supply chain function with Walmart U.S. to streamline operations and leverage enterprise systems and infrastructure.
Walmart serves approximately 280 million customers weekly through more than 10,900 stores in 19 countries, with fiscal 2026 total revenue of $713.2 billion; Walmart U.S. alone operates 4,611 stores.

Walmart announced the Prepaid Consolidation program: suppliers ship under a single national purchase order to one location, where Walmart combines inventory and distributes it across its 42 regional distribution centers, using automated consolidation centers and approved 3PLs (C.H. Robinson, Hub Group, RJW Logistics) at a transparent price-per-case rate.

Walmart and Symbotic announced an expanded commercial agreement to deploy Symbotic A.I.-enabled robotics automation across 25 U.S. regional distribution centers, with an initial $6 billion commitment and $125 million committed for R&D of racking and picking technology.

Walmart opened its fifth next-generation fulfillment center, a 900,000+ sq ft facility in Stockton, CA creating 1,000+ jobs, using advanced automation and machine learning to increase fulfillment capacity and faster delivery across the West Coast.

Walmart signed a multi-year agreement with Zipline to add 300 drone delivery sites nationwide, building on more than 2 million drone deliveries completed to date; 90% of America lives within 10 miles of a Walmart store.

Substantially all Walmart U.S. stores provide same-day pickup and delivery, including expedited options such as in-home delivery; Walmart International offers pickup and delivery from approximately 3,300 locations.
